identity.notes: CoreBluetooth may expose only a per-host peripheral identifier.

methods.notes: Use active scanning and merge advertisement/scan-response names. If no name appears, close the other companion or disable its phone Bluetooth, wake the watch and scan again. Post-connect layout verification is mandatory because only one 2017 firmware generation is hardware-checked upstream.

host_compatibility.basis: ZeTimeConnect's author reports discovery, serial/info and time sync on one 2017-firmware ZeTime using Python/bleak on Windows 11. Other operations were not validated there and are not included in this verdict.

identification.notes: ZeTimeConnect reports names of this form. Its broader case-insensitive ZeTime/Kronoz heuristic is not used as a strong identity rule. Confirm the 6006/8001-8004 GATT layout and read the serial before any write. Do not use old numeric handles: value handles and declaration handles differ by one on some backends; UUIDs are canonical below.

device.name: MyKronoz ZeTime
device.notes:
A hybrid analog/digital watch controlled directly over BLE with no account, cloud key or application-layer encryption. Discovery is by a name such as ZeTime#12345 (digits are only an example). A watch already connected to another phone normally stops advertising, so disconnect that phone before scanning.
The command envelope is 6f | subject | type | payload_length:u16 LE | payload | 8f. Split bodies into writes of at most 20 bytes on characteristic 8001, then write 03 on 8002 to commit. Notifications on 8002 are responses; notifications on 8004 are independent watch-initiated requests. A notification is a fragment, not necessarily a complete frame, and the two streams must never share a reassembly buffer or response queue.

openness.notes: ZeTime is covered, not ZeFit, ZeRound or other models in the vendor SDK. The vendor Android package is delisted; company/service status beyond that is not asserted. Core protocols come from public reverse engineering.

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Connectable whenever awake and not already held by another central; no pairing window or PIN.

exclusivity.notes: Gadgetbridge marks ZeTime pair-free. single_bond is false because no bond is created, not because multiple encrypted bonds are supported.
exclusivity.recovery: Close the vendor app, Gadgetbridge or ZeTimeConnect and disable the old phone's Bluetooth if needed. For an initial install animation, Gadgetbridge reports a long middle-button press may reach calibration. Calibration itself can be entered by long-pressing upper+lower buttons until power-off, then the same combination through the logo until the screen turns black and releasing; this is unverified and not a reset.

pairing.notes: Medium confidence is based on Gadgetbridge's pair-free listing and the working unpaired open client. No project hardware run is claimed.

unpair.notes: There is no BLE bond to revoke; forget any convenience entry in the old app/OS and disconnect.

credentials.notes: No Wi-Fi or application credential exists in the documented path. Radio proximity is the only access control for unpaired reads/writes; protect any exported history as health data.
stored_on_device: Watch settings, analog calibration and activity/sleep/heart-rate history

factory_reset.description: Gadgetbridge describes initial modes and analog calibration, not a reliable full reset. The long upper+lower button sequence enters calibration mode; it is NOT asserted to erase settings, bonds or history and is not listed as a factory reset. No reset bytes are provided.
factory_reset.effect: No full factory-reset procedure or exact data-clearing scope is established.

methods.description: Disconnect the previous phone, scan for ZeTime#..., verify all four characteristics, subscribe to 8002 and 8004, read serial/info, and only then write time. Notification and weather writes remain unverified upstream.

steps.action: Charge and wake the watch; disconnect the phone or IDE already holding it.
steps.expect: The watch advertises a ZeTime#... name.

steps.action: Connect and discover service 00006006-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb and characteristics 8001-8004.
steps.expect: All four UUIDs are present; use UUIDs rather than numeric handles.

steps.action: Subscribe independently to response stream 8002 and spontaneous-request stream 8004.
steps.expect: Each notification is appended only to its own stream buffer.

steps.action: Send read_serial and commit_message, then match a type-80 response with subject 02.
For an unknown unit, stop after read-only checks until its firmware behavior is established.

timing.notes: ATT writes are without response, so ZeTimeConnect leaves 20 ms between chunks. The 4096-byte bound is a defensive implementation limit, not a vendor-advertised protocol maximum; an implausible declared length causes resynchronization rather than allocation.

causes: Another phone is connected; ZeTime normally stops advertising while occupied.
The watch is asleep, or its name is in a scan response rather than the primary advertisement.
It is in an initial install/calibration mode rather than normal operation; see the model-guide cautions below.
troubleshooting.symptom: The watch is absent from scans.

causes: 8002 and 8004 were merged. They are independent streams and require independent buffers/queues.
The commit byte 03 was not written to 8002 after the final 8001 body chunk.
troubleshooting.symptom: A response never arrives or a spontaneous music request is consumed as a reply.

causes: The old fixed suffix 00 00 01 01 00 hard-codes UTC+1. Compute signed timezone hours and absolute offset minutes instead.
troubleshooting.symptom: Time is one or more hours wrong after sync.

causes: Time sync does not calibrate the hands. The analog calibration exchange is not publicly mapped and is outside this spec.
troubleshooting.symptom: Digital time changed but the analog hands did not.

setup.notes: No provisioning or bond is needed for the covered protocol. Medium confidence follows a working open implementation and hardware-checked upstream flow; this project did not repeat it. Initial watch modes are less settled: see the calibration cautions in pairing.exclusivity.recovery and remaining_unknowns.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds a new client. Disconnect the previous phone, optionally forget its OS/app entry, and scan again. If the watch is stuck in its initial install animation, Gadgetbridge reports that a long middle-button press can reach calibration; this was not reproduced consistently and is not a reset.

steps.action: Disconnect or forget the old companion and wake the watch.
Scan, verify the GATT layout and read serial/info from the new client.
steps.expect: The same 12-byte serial and expected history availability response.

testing.notes: This project did not drive a watch. ZeTimeConnect's author reports service discovery, serial/info and time sync working on one 2017-firmware unit from Windows 11; those are upstream reports, not this project's verification.

variants.notes: The only firmware generation hardware-checked by the open client. Gadgetbridge also documents newer weather-mapping behavior; all other generations require service discovery and read-only confirmation before writes.

evidence.app_static_analysis: The archived vendor app 1.8.2 corroborates the model/app generation and presence of shared update constants. No vendor internal names or assets are reproduced and no DFU behavior is inferred from those constants.

artifacts.description: Hardware-checked serial/info/time path and offline stream/time tests; notification/weather/history remain unvalidated.

artifacts.artifact: Gadgetbridge ZeTime protocol analysis and model page
artifacts.description: Public envelope and subject layouts, pair-free support and initial-mode/OTA boundaries.

evidence.negative_findings: No vendor manual/FCC filing was established. Notification/weather writes and raw history were not hardware-validated upstream. Battery, analog calibration and complete watch-request replies remain unimplemented because evidence is insufficient.
evidence.open_questions: Second-firmware behavior, actual weather-day meaning, notification rendering, history pagination/timestamps/calorie units, response formats on 8003, and reset.
evidence.public_implementation: ZeTimeConnect at 22f34c8948e48200904a36bd19d414fdf6bbbd76 supplies UUID-based discovery, 20-byte chunking, the 03 commit, 20 ms pacing, independent stream reassembly, subject matching and computed timezones. Its author reports 16/16 offline tests and hardware success only for discovery/info/time on one unit.
evidence.public_protocol_note: Gadgetbridge's ZeTime protocol page supplies the envelope, subjects, serial/time, history, notification, weather and music layouts. Its model page supplies pair-free support, initial-mode/calibration cautions and the unsupported-OTA boundary.

dfu_mode.notes: Not established; do not probe candidate DFU services.

enter.notes: Nordic/Apollo constants in an archived shared app are not evidence of a safe ZeTime update path and are deliberately not exposed.

image.notes: The archived app fetched OTA images online; no public image or model-safe update flow was established.

dfu.notes: Recorded to keep update access read-only and prevent unsupported OTA claims.

recovery.notes: Gadgetbridge does not support ZeTime firmware update; no recovery behavior is known.

commit_message.description: Single byte 03 on 8002 only after the final 8001 chunk of the same message.

query_history_availability.description: Subject 52/type 70; response carries four u16 LE pending-record counts.

read_activity_page.description: Read one activity record page (subject 54); raw history was not collected upstream.

read_heart_rate_page.description: Read one heart-rate record page (subject 61); raw history was not collected upstream.

read_serial.description: Subject 02/type 70 with one zero payload byte; response is 12 ASCII bytes on 8002.

read_sleep_page.description: Read one sleep event page (subject 56); raw history was not collected upstream.

set_time.description: Subject 04/type 71 with a 12-byte local-time/timezone payload. Commit on 8002; does not calibrate analog hands.

write_sequence: Build the complete 6f envelope, then write it to 8001 in ordered chunks of at most 20 bytes with 20 ms between writes.
Only after the last 8001 chunk, write single byte 03 to 8002. The commit is sequenced, not an independent executable command.
Reassemble 8002 responses and 8004 watch requests in separate buffers, then match subject/type as described in envelope.

envelope.commit: After all <=20-byte body chunks on 8001, write single byte 03 on 8002.
receive: Maintain independent bytearrays for 8002 responses and 8004 watch requests.
Discard bytes before the next 6f. Wait for five header bytes, then compute total = 6 + payload_length.
If total exceeds 4096, drop only the current 6f and rescan. If the terminator is not 8f, drop only the current 6f and rescan.
A complete valid frame may be followed immediately by another frame in the same notification. Preserve any trailing partial frame.
Match a response by expected subject and type 80; an unknown subject/type is surfaced as an unrelated frame, never as the awaited result.

fields.name: calories
fields.notes: Unit not established; do not label kcal.

history.support_boundary: Layouts are from Gadgetbridge's public protocol note. No activity, sleep or heart-rate history was downloaded by this research, and ZeTimeConnect leaves these raw. Do not claim complete history sync, deletion, or duplicate handling.

initial_modes.notes: Gadgetbridge describes barcode/serial, install-animation, calibration and normal modes. Only normal mode exposes the complete support surface. A long middle-button press may skip the install animation; upper+lower-button calibration sequences are not factory resets and were not consistently reproduced upstream.

replies.simple_status: status byte (00 playing / 01 paused) + UTF-8 title

music.stream_role: Requests may arrive spontaneously on 8004; answers belong on 8003 and their full formats are not all known.

notification.call_boundary: Type 06 ends an incoming-call alert; failing to send it can leave the watch ringing.
notification.limits: Truncate each UTF-8 title/body to at most 255 bytes without splitting a code point; count bytes, not characters.
notification.support_boundary: Payload write was NOT validated by ZeTimeConnect and is not exposed as a generic command/entity. It is an implementable candidate requiring an owner-approved test.

out_of_scope: Battery read, analog-hand calibration, user profile/goals and full watch-request response formats.
Firmware update commands and DFU UUID probing.
ZeFit, ZeRound and other vendor models; other ZeTime firmware without read-only confirmation.
Complete history sync/deletion and multi-day weather semantics.

serial.response: 12 ASCII bytes; no terminator. The public hardware regression uses only replaced digits.

time_sync.analog_hands: Not calibrated by this command; their separate calibration exchange is unknown.

values.0: 24-hour format used by the open client
value used by the open client

values.1: value used by the open client

fields.name: timezone_minute
fields.notes: Absolute minute remainder, including for negative offsets.

time_sync.old_suffix_warning: The public prose constant 00 00 01 01 00 encodes UTC+1 and is not valid globally.
time_sync.timezone_rule: total_minutes = local UTC offset in minutes; hour = trunc(total_minutes / 60) toward zero; minute = abs(total_minutes) % 60.

weather.envelope: Four consecutive 5-byte day blocks followed by unterminated UTF-8 location bytes.
weather.support_boundary: Weather writes were NOT validated by ZeTimeConnect. The public envelope has current plus three daily blocks, but exact J+1/J+2/J+3 semantics are unresolved. The open client's repeated-one-forecast workaround is not declared correct and is intentionally omitted. Current-day write requires owner validation; multi-day forecasting is not implementable from this document alone.
weather.test_vector: A synthetic single block 00 12 05 15 01 means 18 C, min 5 C, max 21 C, cloudy; this tests widths only, not forecast correctness.

remaining_unknowns: Behavior on firmware other than the one 2017 unit hardware-checked upstream.
Notification rendering and exact multi-day weather semantics; neither write was validated by the open client.
History pagination, duplicate handling, calorie units, epoch timezone and complete availability semantics.
Analog-hand calibration, battery read, user profiles/goals and all 8003 response formats.
A factory-reset procedure and exactly what it clears.

characteristics.name: Message body writes
characteristics.notes: Documentation-only body channel. A dedicated session handler must perform ordered <=20-byte writes, pacing, the later 8002 commit and reassembly. No isolated command or bare framing is exposed.

format.name: payload_length
format.notes: 12 for serial; reject inconsistent frame length.

format.name: serial
format.notes: ASCII, no terminator. Example vectors use an invented serial.

format_match.notes: Serial response only; other subjects use protocol_details layouts.

characteristics.name: Commit and response notifications
characteristics.notes: Phone writes 03 only after the final 8001 chunk of the same logical message; it is not an independent command. Watch responses arrive fragmented here. Match response subject and type 80 to the request; ignore late/unrelated subjects instead of consuming them as the current response.

characteristics.name: Answers to watch-initiated requests
characteristics.notes: Phone answers 8004 requests here. Response formats are not sufficiently known; no writes or commands are declared. Do not reuse 8001 for this role.

characteristics.name: Spontaneous watch requests
characteristics.notes: Music/find-phone/call actions initiated by the watch. Keep this stream separate from 8002 and read protocol_details.music before responding on 8003.

initialization.notes: Response stream; reassemble frames independently of 8004.
Spontaneous watch requests; never consume as command responses.
